newsitem.title: USA: Claridge in talks to be acquired by Hilton.
newsitem.headline: Claridge in talks to be acquired by Hilton.

text.p: Claridge Hotel and Casino Corp. said Friday it is in talks to be acquired by Hilton Hotels Corp., a major bondholder, as a way to rescue the company from a potential default on debt payments and bankruptcy.
Hilton, which holds between 35 percent and 40 percent of Claridge's outstanding notes, is at the same time formalising a $6.5 billion hostile bid for ITT Corp.
Claridge, a closely held corporation, also said it will not make the interest payment due Feb. 3 on its 11-3/4 percent first mortgage notes, which mature in 2002. This would constitute a default.
The company said it believes it is highly unlikely that it will make the payment within the 30-day period.
Claridge, which operates the Claridge Casino Hotel in Atlantic City, N.J., is in the process of formulating a prepackaged plan of reorganization.
An acquisition by Hilton would be through a prepackaged bankruptcy plan, it said.
Under such a plan, Hilton would acquire all of the stock in Claridge in exchange for Hilton funding a cash distribution to the holders of its notes.
Hilton representatives are in discussions with Claridge's financial adviser, Dillon, Read & Co., Claridge said. It said there are no assurances that a deal will be made.
Hilton, the nation's largest hotel and gambling company, made its surprise offer for ITT on Monday and plans to formalise the bid by the end of the week.
